title: Brewing or distilling dregs and waste

review.classification: The retained UNSD complete notes on PDF pp. 199–200 identify 39160 for brewing or distilling dregs and waste. Dry-milling bran, starch residues, sugar residues and wine lees occupy distinct classes. Independently checked product evidence establishes that the chosen whole wet solids come from beer wort separation and are commercially supplied for feed.
review.state_and_route: The KW source directly describes moist single-ingredient bulk supply from malted barley brewing. The Brewers Association documents separated spent grain along with separate yeast and filter-medium streams. The process equipment original supports optional wet dewatering. Study-specific lot history, mill/wort interface, receiving specification and feed release are required.
review.quantity_and_allocation: English and Chinese agree on measured wet first release, non-additive wet/dry measurements, matched transfers, original FG cohorts, new rework loads and zero-output periods. The upstream vector is inherited once. Checked page 55 Table 21 and footnote 17 in the retained Beer PEFCR revision. Its beer reporting rule cannot establish zero environmental impact for the wet grain leaving the brewery.
review.native_and_bilingual: Verified the canonical archived Mass and kg link against pinned tree digests and extracted the reference unit. The method exposes 57 unbound flow-row identities with actual facility and supplier data requirements. Its two language editions have equivalent eligibility and numerical structure, and require compatible flow and provider evidence for application.

sources.first_title_line: Brewing or distilling dregs and waste

sources.role: Original feed merchant specification. Moist single feed, malted barley origin and bulk hand-off are evidenced. Typical composition remains illustrative.
Industry primary technical guidance for distinct spent grain, yeast and filter streams and actual transfer/collection.
Equipment origin demonstrating wet collection and optional mechanical dewatering, with separate dry or mixed routes.
Table 21 footnote 17 on printed page 55 limits the no-allocation rule and explicitly excludes exported grain impacts from that convention.
